summary: Repeated Swarm control failures are now reproducibly caused by worker lifecycle vocabulary drift rather than the merged #298 health-fence patch itself. Exact-head run 31470824438 failed on sol-20260811-z5p8c3, and run 31470893878 then failed on sol-20260811-h8v5c1 with status CLAIMING. Canonical swarmctl accepts only WORKING, WAITING, REVIEWING, INTEGRATING, BLOCKED, IDLE, STOPPED, while Docs/SWARM_PROTOCOL.md tells every Go worker to register before claiming but does not publish the accepted worker-status vocabulary. A narrow recovery lane now exists to make that lifecycle contract explicit and test it. SWARM-PROTOCOL is currently owned by generation-2 health-fence recovery sol-20260811-s5q8m4, so no competing protected implementation was started.
evidence: Actions run 31470824438: core 23 tests and hardening 17 tests passed, then live-state validation failed with invalid worker status on sol-20260811-z5p8c3.
Actions run 31470893878: the same 23 plus 17 tests passed, then live-state validation failed with invalid worker status on sol-20260811-h8v5c1; its live record uses CLAIMING.
tools/swarm/swarmctl.py defines WORKER_STATUSES as WORKING, WAITING, REVIEWING, INTEGRATING, BLOCKED, IDLE, STOPPED.
Docs/SWARM_PROTOCOL.md requires register worker before atomic claim but does not enumerate legal worker status values, making CLAIMING a predictable worker-authored state.
SWARM-PROTOCOL generation-2 lease was acquired by sol-20260811-s5q8m4 at 2026-08-11T07:54:41+00:00, so this worker remained read-only on the protected contract.

acceptance: document the supported worker lifecycle vocabulary where every Go worker reads it
cover the intended registration-to-claim status contract in control-plane tests
retain fail-closed rejection for genuinely unknown statuses
reconcile live malformed worker records without stealing an active SWARM-PROTOCOL lease
